## Key Insights

The framework must supervise the provider process at the actual execution boundary. A worker heartbeat and provider progress are different facts; output silence is diagnostic rather than terminal. Every wait must be bounded, every run must have a finite absolute deadline, and a durable next-touch reconciler must be able to materialize terminal truth even when the original worker becomes wedged. Formal reviewer evidence must bind to the exact managed receipt instead of provider plus story plus time-window guesses.

Reviewer evidence also needs a two-phase provenance protocol. The provider reviewer authors an immutable proposal containing its pass/findings and truthful read evidence while the run is active. It cannot call the final evidence writer before the terminal receipt and evidence journal are sealed. After successful terminal, a mechanical importer validates the sealed proposal and imports it without allowing the controller to change the verdict or become the reviewer. A single deep ManagedHostRun module adds durable runtime artifacts, worker continuation and reconciliation complexity, but removes duplicated foreground/background supervision and makes cancellation, cleanup and evidence semantics consistent.
